inspiration: Tray-plus-window dashboard: the client is a background tool with a system tray entry (stated in docs/gui-dashboard.md). The window panels are inferred from file names (status, counters, activity, log tail in internal/dashboard/ and frontend/src/lib/). Recreate: a status-first panel for a long-running helper tool.

Status as one source of truth: the dashboard package holds one state object that the rest of the app writes into, with no UI framework inside (docs/gui-dashboard.md). Recreate: a single state holder for any HUD or helper overlay, so the screen reads from one place.

Counters plus activity: separate counter and activity modules feed the panel, which keeps the UI simple (internal/dashboard/counters.go, activity.go). Recreate: a small counter strip for in-game statistics feeding a rolling event list.
Log tail as a debug panel: a log hook feeds a live tail view (internal/dashboard/loghook.go, frontend/src/lib/LogTail.svelte). Recreate: an in-game developer log panel with the same hook pattern.

Icon source kept with the build: the icon source file (.psd) and a make script sit beside the shipped .ico and .png (icon/make_icon.sh). Recreate: keep editable art sources and the export script in the repo so icons can be rebuilt.
